verses.zh: 天上现出大异象来：有一个妇人身披日头，脚踏月亮，头戴十二星的冠冕。
verses.en: Then[NOTE:1] a great sign appeared in heaven: a woman clothed with the sun, and with the moon under her feet, and on her head was a crown of twelve stars.[NOTE:2]
notes: Here καί (kai) has been translated as “then” to indicate the implied sequence within the narrative.
Sun…moon…stars. This imagery is frequently identified with the nation Israel because of Joseph’s dream in Gen 37.

verses.zh: 她怀了孕，在生产的艰难中疼痛呼叫。
verses.en: She[NOTE:1] was pregnant and was screaming in labor pains, struggling[NOTE:2] to give birth.
notes: Here καί (kai) has not been translated because of differences between Greek and English style.

Grk “and being tortured,” though βασανίζω (basanizō) in this context refers to birth pangs. BDAG 168 s.v. 2.b states, “Of birth-pangs (Anth. Pal. 9, 311 βάσανος has this mng.) Rv 12:2.” The καί (kai) has not been translated.

verses.zh: 天上又现出异象来：有一条大红龙，七头十角；七头上戴着七个冠冕。
verses.en: Then[NOTE:1] another sign appeared in heaven: a huge red dragon that had seven heads and ten horns, and on its heads were seven diadem crowns.[NOTE:2]
notes: Here καί (kai) has been translated as “then” to indicate the implied sequence of events within the vision.

For the translation of διάδημα (diadēma) as “diadem crown” see L&N 6.196.sn Diadem crowns were a type of crown used as a symbol of the highest ruling authority in a given area, and thus often associated with kingship.

verses.zh: 它的尾巴拖拉着天上星辰的三分之一，摔在地上。龙就站在那将要生产的妇人面前，等她生产之后，要吞吃她的孩子。
verses.en: Now[NOTE:1] the dragon’s[NOTE:2] tail swept away a third of the stars in heaven and hurled them to the earth. Then[NOTE:3] the dragon stood before the woman who was about to give birth, so that he might devour her child as soon as it was born.
notes: Here καί (kai) has been translated as “now” to indicate that this remark is virtually parenthetical.
Grk “its”; the referent (the dragon) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
Here καί (kai) has been translated as “then” to indicate the implied sequence of events within the vision.

verses.zh: 妇人生了一个男孩子，是将来要用铁杖辖管（辖管：原文是牧）万国的；她的孩子被提到　神宝座那里去了。
verses.en: So[NOTE:1] the woman gave birth to a son, a male child,[NOTE:2] who is going to rule[NOTE:3] over all the nations[NOTE:4] with an iron rod.[NOTE:5] Her[NOTE:6] child was suddenly caught up to God and to his throne,
notes: Here καί (kai) has been translated as “so” to indicate the conclusion of the anticipated birth.

On this term BDAG 135 s.v. ἄρσην states: “male…The neut. ἄρσεν Rv 12:5, difft. vs. 13, comes fr. Is 66:7 and is in apposition to υἱόν. On the juxtaposition s. FBoll, ZNW 15, 1914, 253; BOlsson, Glotta 23, ’34, 112.”
Grk “shepherd.”
Or “all the Gentiles” (the same Greek word may be translated “Gentiles” or “nations”).
Or “scepter.” The Greek term ῥάβδος (rhabdos) can mean either “rod” or “scepter.” sn An allusion to Ps 2:9 (see also Rev 2:27; 19:15).
Here καί (kai) has not been translated because of differences between Greek and English style.

verses.zh: 妇人就逃到旷野，在那里有　神给她预备的地方，使她被养活一千二百六十天。
verses.en: and she[NOTE:1] fled into the wilderness[NOTE:2] where a place had been prepared for her[NOTE:3] by God, so she could be taken care of[NOTE:4] for 1,260 days.
notes: Grk “and the woman,” which would be somewhat redundant in English.
Or “desert.”
Grk “where she has there a place prepared by God.”
Grk “so they can take care of her.”

verses.zh: 在天上就有了争战。米迦勒同他的使者与龙争战，龙也同它的使者去争战，
verses.en: Then[NOTE:1] war broke out in heaven: Michael[NOTE:2] and his angels fought against the dragon, and the dragon and his angels fought back.
notes: Here καί (kai) has been translated as “then” to indicate the implied sequence within the narrative.
The archangel Michael had a special role in protecting the nation of Israel in the OT (Dan 10:13, 21; 12:1; see also Jude 9).

verses.zh: 并没有得胜，天上再没有它们的地方。
verses.en: But[NOTE:1] the dragon was not strong enough to prevail,[NOTE:2] so there was no longer any place left[NOTE:3] in heaven for him and his angels.[NOTE:4]
notes: Here καί (kai) has been translated as “but” to indicate the implied contrast.
The words “to prevail” are not in the Greek text, but are implied.
Grk “found.”
Grk “for them”; the referent (the dragon and his angels, v. 7) has been specified in the translation for clarity.

verses.zh: 大龙就是那古蛇，名叫魔鬼，又叫撒但，是迷惑普天下的。它被摔在地上，它的使者也一同被摔下去。
verses.en: So[NOTE:1] that huge dragon—the ancient serpent, the one called the devil and Satan, who deceives the whole world—was thrown down to the earth, and his angels along with him.
notes: Here καί (kai) has been translated as “so” to indicate the result of the war in heaven.

verses.zh: 我听见在天上有大声音说：「我　神的救恩、能力、国度，并他基督的权柄，现在都来到了！因为那在我们　神面前昼夜控告我们弟兄的，已经被摔下去了。
verses.en: Then[NOTE:1] I heard a loud voice in heaven saying,“The salvation and the powerand the kingdom of our God, and the ruling authority[NOTE:2] of his Christ,[NOTE:3] have now come, because the accuser of our brothers and sisters,[NOTE:4] the one who accuses them day and night[NOTE:5] before our God, has been thrown down.
notes: Here καί (kai) has been translated as “then” to indicate the implied sequence of events within the vision.
Or “the right of his Messiah to rule.” See L&N 37.35.
Or “Messiah”; both “Christ” (Greek) and “Messiah” (Hebrew and Aramaic) mean “one who has been anointed.”

Grk “brothers,” but the Greek word may be used for “brothers and sisters” or “fellow Christians” (cf. BDAG 18 s.v. ἀδελφός 1, where considerable nonbiblical evidence for the plural ἀδελφοί [adelphoi] meaning “brothers and sisters” is cited). The translation “fellow believer” would normally apply (L&N 11.23), but since the speaker(s) are not specified in this context, it is not clear if such a translation would be appropriate here. The more generic “brothers and sisters” was chosen to emphasize the fact of a relationship without specifying its type.
Or “who accuses them continually.”

verses.zh: 弟兄胜过它，是因羔羊的血和自己所见证的道。他们虽至于死，也不爱惜性命。
verses.en: But[NOTE:1] they overcame him by the blood of the Lamband by the word of their testimony,and they did not love their lives[NOTE:2] so much that they were afraid to die.
notes: Here καί (kai) has been translated as “but” to indicate the contrast.
They did not love their lives. See Matt 16:25; Luke 17:33; John 12:25.

verses.zh: 所以，诸天和住在其中的，你们都快乐吧！只是地与海有祸了！因为魔鬼知道自己的时候不多，就气忿忿地下到你们那里去了。」
verses.en: Therefore you heavens rejoice, and all who reside in them!But[NOTE:1] woe to the earth and the sea because the devil has come down to you! He[NOTE:2] is filled with terrible anger, for he knows that he only has a little time!”
notes: The word “But” is not in the Greek text, but the contrast is clearly implied. This is a case of asyndeton (lack of a connective).

Grk “and is filled,” a continuation of the previous sentence. Because English tends to use shorter sentences (especially when exclamations are involved), a new sentence was started here in the translation.

verses.zh: 龙见自己被摔在地上，就逼迫那生男孩子的妇人。
verses.en: Now[NOTE:1] when the dragon realized[NOTE:2] that he had been thrown down to the earth, he pursued the woman who had given birth to the male child.
notes: Here καί (kai) has been translated as “now” because the clause it introduces is clearly resumptive.
Grk “saw.”

verses.zh: 于是有大鹰的两个翅膀赐给妇人，叫她能飞到旷野，到自己的地方，躲避那蛇；她在那里被养活一载二载半载。
verses.en: But[NOTE:1] the woman was given the two wings of a giant eagle so that she could fly out into the wilderness,[NOTE:2] to the place God[NOTE:3] prepared for her, where she is taken care of—away from the presence of the serpent—for a time, times, and half a time.[NOTE:4]
notes: Here καί (kai) has been translated as “but” to indicate the contrast present here.
Or “desert.”
The word “God” is supplied based on the previous statements made concerning “the place prepared for the woman” in 12:6.

The reading “and half a time” (καὶ ἥμισυ καιροῦ, kai hēmisu kairou) is lacking in the significant majuscule C. Its inclusion, however, is supported by P47 א A and the rest of the ms tradition. There is apparently no reason for the scribe of C to intentionally omit the phrase, and the fact that the word “time” (καιρὸν καὶ καιρούς, kairon kai kairous) appears twice before may indicate a scribal oversight.sn The parallel statement in Rev 12:6 suggests that the phrase a time, times, and half a time equals 1,260 days (three and a half years of 360 days each).

verses.zh: 蛇就在妇人身后，从口中吐出水来，像河一样，要将妇人冲去。
verses.en: Then[NOTE:1] the serpent spouted water like a river out of his mouth after the woman in an attempt to[NOTE:2] sweep her away by a flood,
notes: Here καί (kai) has been translated as “then” to indicate the implied sequence of events within the vision.
Grk “so that he might make her swept away.”

verses.zh: 地却帮助妇人，开口吞了从龙口吐出来的水（原文是河）。
verses.en: but[NOTE:1] the earth came to her rescue;[NOTE:2] the ground opened up[NOTE:3] and swallowed the river that the dragon had spewed from his mouth.
notes: Here καί (kai) has been translated as “but” to indicate the contrast present here.
Grk “the earth helped the woman.”
Grk “the earth opened its mouth” (a metaphor for the ground splitting open).

verses.zh: 龙向妇人发怒，去与她其余的儿女争战，这儿女就是那守　神诫命、为耶稣作见证的。
verses.en: So[NOTE:1] the dragon became enraged at the woman and went away to make war on the rest of her children,[NOTE:2] those who keep[NOTE:3] God’s commandments and hold to[NOTE:4] the testimony about Jesus.[NOTE:5] (12:18) And the dragon[NOTE:6] stood[NOTE:7] on the sand[NOTE:8] of the seashore.[NOTE:9]
notes: Here καί (kai) has been translated as “so” to indicate the implied result of the woman’s escape.
Grk “her seed” (an idiom for offspring, children, or descendants).
Or “who obey.”
Grk “and having.”
Grk “the testimony of Jesus,” which may involve a subjective genitive (“Jesus’ testimony”) or, more likely, an objective genitive (“testimony about Jesus”).
Grk “he”; the referent (the dragon) has been specified in the translation for clarity.

Grk ἐστάθη (estathē, “he stood”). The reading followed by the translation is attested by the better mss (P47 א A C 1854 2344 2351 lat syh) while the majority of mss (051 M vgmss syph co) have the reading ἐστάθην (estathēn, “I stood”). Thus, the majority of mss make the narrator, rather than the dragon of 12:17, the subject of the verb. The first person reading is most likely an assimilation to the following verb in 13:1, “I saw.” The reading “I stood” was introduced either by accident or to produce a smoother flow, giving the narrator a vantage point on the sea’s edge from which to observe the beast rising out of the sea in 13:1. But almost everywhere else in the book, the phrase καὶ εἶδον (kai eidon, “and I saw”) marks a transition to a new vision, without reference to the narrator’s activity. On both external and internal grounds, it is best to adopt the third person reading, “he stood.”
Or “sandy beach” (L&N 1.64).

The standard critical texts of the Greek NT, NA28 and UBS5, both include this sentence as 12:18, as do the RSV and NRSV. Other modern translations like the NASB and NIV include the sentence at the beginning of 13:1; in these versions chap. 12 has only 17 verses.

verses.zh: 那时龙就站在海边的沙上。
